title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 46
paragraphs: Then the Athenian generals came to the right wing and reported to Pausanias what they had heard from Alexander. At this, he, struck with fear of the Persians, spoke as follows: “Since, then, the battle comes on at dawn, it is right that you Athenians take your stand opposite the Persians, and we opposite the Boeotians and those Greeks now posted against you. The reason is that you are acquainted with the Medes and their manner of fighting, having fought them at Marathon, while we have no experience of these men and are ignorant of them; for not one Spartan has tested himself against the Medes in combat, though we have experience of the Boeotians and the Thessalians. It is right, therefore, that you take up your arms and come to this wing, and we go to the left.” To this the Athenians answered: “To us also, long ago at the very first, when we saw the Persians being drawn up opposite you, it occurred to say these very things, which you now bring forward before we have uttered them; but we feared that these words might not please you. Since, however, you yourselves have mentioned this, know that your words have given us pleasure, and that we are ready to do what you propose.”
